source_read: the product pages on https://www.costa.co.uk/menu/<slug> (each prints 'Nutritional Information (UK)' and 'Allergens Information (UK)'); robots.txt of costa.co.uk was read before the first read
method: Independent second read in the founder's Chrome with get_page_text on each product page (the first read used find/read_page): 15 rows drawn at random (seed 21) from data/source/costa, covering food, hot and iced drinks, teas and biscuits; every printed number (kJ, kcal, fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein, salt, fibre), the portion size text and the allergen 'Yes' words were compared with items.csv.
sample: Iced Mocha - Medium, semi-skimmed milk, Signature blend
Iced Latte - Medium, semi-skimmed milk, Signature blend
Matcha Latte - Medium, semi-skimmed milk, in store
Maple Hazel Hot Chocolate - Medium, semi-skimmed milk, take-out
Iced Caramel Macchiato - Small, semi-skimmed milk, Signature blend, in store
result: 15 of 15 rows match on every number and allergen. Portion text such as 'Per Portion (158ml)' for a bap and '(48ml)' for a biscuit is printed that way by Costa and is copied as printed. The two drinks without allergens listed (Decaf Tea, Mint Tea) print an empty allergen list, which is why those rows carry NONE.
